      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "1.  Purpose and Scope",
      "url": "https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/government-functional-standard-govs-005-digital/government-functional-standard-govs-005-digital-html#purpose-and-scope",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "url": "https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/government-functional-standard-govs-005-digital/government-functional-standard-govs-005-digital-html#purpose-and-scope",
        "text": "\u003ch3 id=\"purpose-of-this-standard\"\u003e1.1  Purpose of this standard\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp\u003eThis standard sets out what government organisations shall do to govern, deliver and assure digital and data activity. It helps organisations improve public services, work more efficiently and manage risk.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eOrganisations shall use a consistent approach so digital and data activity:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003esupports agreed policy and mission outcomes\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003emakes public services easier to access, use and improve\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eimproves productivity and efficiency across government\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003esupports services and platforms that work together, can scale and are resilient\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003euses data to make decisions and improve continuously\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003eThis standard is for:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003esenior accountable leaders, including permanent secretaries, directors general and chief executives of arm’s length bodies\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003esenior leaders accountable for digital and data, including chief digital and information officers and chief data officers\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003esenior leaders responsible for strategy, policy or service delivery\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003epractitioners who plan, deliver, operate or manage digital and data activity\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"scope-of-this-standard\"\u003e1.2  Scope of this standard\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp\u003eThis standard applies to the whole lifecycle of government digital and data activity. This includes planning, designing, delivering, running and retiring:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003epublic-facing and internal services\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003etechnology and platforms\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003edata and data products\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003eThis standard shall apply to government departments, arm’s length bodies and any other organisation in scope of a government functional standard.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eGovS 005 addresses the governance, delivery, operation, resilience and lifecycle management of digital services, data and technology.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eCyber security requirements, controls and assurance expectations are set through GovS 007: Security.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eOrganisations should apply both standards together to ensure digital resilience and cyber security are managed coherently.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eOther public sector organisations, including devolved administrations and local government, may adopt this standard or use it to support benchmarking and improvement.\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"government-standards-references\"\u003e1.3  Government standards references\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp\u003eOrganisations should use this standard with other relevant government functional standards set out on GOV UK. Each standard should be applied according to its own scope and accountabilities. \u003csup id=\"fnref:1\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"#fn:1\" class=\"footnote\" rel=\"footnote\" role=\"doc-noteref\"\u003e[footnote 1]\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/sup\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eThis standard is supported by The Service Standard \u003csup id=\"fnref:2\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"#fn:2\" class=\"footnote\" rel=\"footnote\" role=\"doc-noteref\"\u003e[footnote 2]\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/sup\u003e, which sets expectations for services, and the Technology Code of Practice \u003csup id=\"fnref:3\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"#fn:3\" class=\"footnote\" rel=\"footnote\" role=\"doc-noteref\"\u003e[footnote 3]\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/sup\u003e, which sets expectations for technology decisions.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe following Functional Standards are directly necessary for the use of this standard:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eGovS 002, Project delivery\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eGovS 003, Human resources\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eGovS 006, Finance\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eGovS 007, Security\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eGovS 008, Commercial\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eGovS 009, Internal audit\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eGovS 010, Analysis\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eGovS 013, Counter fraud\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003eTogether, these standards explain how government digital and data activity shall be governed, delivered, secured, measured and assured.\u003c/p\u003e"
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "2.  Principles",
      "url": "https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/government-functional-standard-govs-005-digital/government-functional-standard-govs-005-digital-html#principles",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "url": "https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/government-functional-standard-govs-005-digital/government-functional-standard-govs-005-digital-html#principles",
        "text": "\u003cp\u003eThese principles set the expectations for how government digital and data activity should be planned, governed, delivered and improved to achieve user-centred, secure and measurable public outcomes.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eThey should provide clarity between organisational objectives, accountable delivery, proportionate assurance and continuous improvement across the full service and product lifecycle.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eTo strengthen their impact, the principles should be applied as strategic expectations, supported by evidence of ownership, risk management, performance, interoperability, data governance and ethical practice.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eAnyone responsible for planning, developing, delivering or managing government digital and data activity shall ensure:\u003c/p\u003e\u003col\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003edigital and data activity is aligned with government priorities, organisational objectives and the outcomes needed by users and the public\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003egovernance, assurance and decision making are proportionate to the scale, stage and risk of the work\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eaccountability, ownership and responsibilities are clear across organisational and delivery boundaries\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\u003cp\u003e4. services and products are designed around evidenced user needs, accessibility, inclusion and measurable outcomes\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e5. services, products and technology are managed throughout their lifecycle using evidence, feedback and performance data\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e6. technology and data are managed securely, lawfully and ethically, with appropriate controls for resilience, interoperability and reuse\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e7. teams have the skills, capacity and authority needed to deliver effectively and uphold public service values and professional standards\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e8. options and decisions are informed by a proportionate analysis of uncertainty, including risks, opportunities, assumptions and dependencies, taking into account the chances of different degrees of success or failure\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003e9. government digital and data activity delivers value for money, in alignment with Managing Public Money, securing the appropriate combination of economy, efficiency and effectiveness needed to achieve the intended outcome\u003c/p\u003e"
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "3.  Context",
      "url": "https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/government-functional-standard-govs-005-digital/government-functional-standard-govs-005-digital-html#context",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "url": "https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/government-functional-standard-govs-005-digital/government-functional-standard-govs-005-digital-html#context",
        "text": "\u003ch3 id=\"introduction\"\u003e3.1  Introduction\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp\u003eThis section explains the context for applying this functional standard. It sets out how government digital and data capabilities support policy outcomes, improve services, strengthen assurance, manage risk and help organisations work better.\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"digital-transformation\"\u003e3.2  Digital transformation\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp\u003eDigital transformation means improving how government designs, delivers and manages services. Services should be simple, accessible, secure and efficient for users and organisations.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eThis includes improving whole services and processes, using data well, and making sure technology is secure, sustainable, interoperable and aligned to user and policy needs.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eEffective delivery needs clear ownership across the lifecycle, multidisciplinary working and continuous improvement across services, technology and data. This means:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eidentifying accountable owners for services, products, technology and data across their lifecycle\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eusing multidisciplinary teams to work across organisational boundaries, improve outcomes, manage risk, measure performance and improve delivery\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"services\"\u003e3.3  Services\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp\u003eA service helps users achieve an outcome. It should reflect policy intent, legal requirements, operational needs and user needs.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eServices can be public facing, such as applying for a licence, or internal, such as platforms that support finance, human resources or case management.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eA service can include digital and non-digital parts that work together across the whole user journey. Digital parts can include online forms, notifications, application programming interfaces and casework tools. Non-digital parts can include assisted digital support, post, telephone contact and face-to-face interactions.\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"technology\"\u003e3.4  Technology\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp\u003eTechnology means the systems, platforms, infrastructure, applications and tools used to deliver, run, secure and improve government services and organisational capabilities.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eThis includes physical and cloud infrastructure, networks, end-user devices, hosting environments and other components used to create, process, store, secure and share information.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eThis includes artificial intelligence technologies. Organisations should select, buy, deploy and manage them safely, securely and responsibly, with clear lifecycle ownership, assurance, proportionate risk management and meaningful human control at the right stages.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eTechnology also includes software, applications, integrations, automation and code used to:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eprovide interfaces for users, staff and other systems\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003esupport policy delivery, operational processes, service management and decision making\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"data\"\u003e3.5  Data\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp\u003eData is information that government collects, creates, uses, shares and manages. It helps government understand needs, make decisions, deliver services, monitor performance, manage risk and improve outcomes.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eWhere data supports artificial intelligence tools, organisations should make sure it is lawful, relevant, accurate, secure and properly governed. They should identify and manage risks relating to privacy, fairness, bias, transparency and information quality.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eTypes of data include:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003epersonal data, such as names, contact details and identifiers\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003elocation and environmental data, such as geospatial reference data\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eadministrative and operational data about organisations, assets, services and transactions\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003eUses for data include:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003einform policy design, development, implementation and evaluation\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003emonitor and report on performance, outcomes, risk and value for money\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003esupport service delivery and improvement, including eligibility checks, case management and service analytics\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ehelp organisations understand performance, manage risk and make evidence-based decisions\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003eOrganisations applying this standard should treat services, technology and data as connected parts of one delivery system. They should build clear ownership, proportionate assurance and continuous improvement into how they plan, deliver and manage outcomes.\u003c/p\u003e"
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "4.  Governance",
      "url": "https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/government-functional-standard-govs-005-digital/government-functional-standard-govs-005-digital-html#governance",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "url": "https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/government-functional-standard-govs-005-digital/government-functional-standard-govs-005-digital-html#governance",
        "text": "\u003ch3 id=\"governance-and-management-framework\"\u003e4.1  Governance and management framework\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ch4 id=\"overview\"\u003e4.1.1  Overview\u003c/h4\u003e\u003cp\u003eGovernance covers prioritising, authorising, empowering, overseeing and assuring performance across government and within each organisation.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eA governance and management framework shall be defined by those accountable for government digital and data activity. It should ensure governance is effective, proportionate, structured and aligned with cross-government priorities, including the safe, secure and responsible use of artificial intelligence.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eIt should include:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003edelegated authority limits, decision-making roles and rules, assurance needs, reporting structures, accountabilities and escalation routes\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003emanagement practices and documentation needed to meet this standard, including records of significant digital, data and AI-enabled systems where appropriate\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003erisk appetite and tolerance, risk ownership, reporting, oversight and escalation arrangements within the governance and management framework\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003ch4 id=\"governance-across-government\"\u003e4.1.2  Governance across government\u003c/h4\u003e\u003cp\u003eA senior officer accountable for government digital and data strategy and planning across government shall be assigned (see 4.6.2). They should define the cross-government governance and management framework in consultation with organisational digital and data leaders (see 4.6.4).\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe cross-government governance and management framework should include:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003earrangements for developing and monitoring cross-government digital strategies and plans (see 4.2.1)\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ecross-government service, technology and data standards\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ecapability requirements\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eguidance for practitioners\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eexpectations for responsible AI adoption\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003earrangements for identifying, assessing and managing systemic digital, data and technology risks\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003ch4 id=\"governance-within-each-organisation\"\u003e4.1.3  Governance within each organisation\u003c/h4\u003e\u003cp\u003eGovernance of government digital and data work within an organisation should be integrated with the organisation’s overall governance. The framework should bring together digital, data, service, technology, AI and wider business leaders so that work is prioritised, funded, delivered and improved in line with organisational objectives.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eEach organisation’s governance and management framework should comply with:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003egovernment and departmental policies\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ethis functional standard and other relevant functional standards (see 1.2)\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ecross-government standards and requirements (see 4.1.2)\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eapplicable AI guidance, ethics requirements, data protection obligations, security standards and assurance expectations\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003estatutory requirements\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003eAs part of the governance and management framework, each organisation should develop and maintain:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003erequired strategies and plans (see 4.2)\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ea pipeline of proposed, current and completed work, including associated spend\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003eA senior officer accountable for the governance of the organisation’s government digital and data portfolio shall be assigned (see 4.6.4).\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"strategy-and-planning\"\u003e4.2  Strategy and planning\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ch4 id=\"cross-government-digital-strategy\"\u003e4.2.1  Cross-government digital strategy\u003c/h4\u003e\u003cp\u003eA cross-government strategy shall be developed and maintained to set the ambition for modern digital government and guide government digital and data work in organisations. It should reach at least three to five years into the future and set expectations for:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003esynergy, efficiency and interoperability of government digital and data activity, services, technology, data and related assets within and among organisations\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eidentifying and managing principal and systemic digital, data and technology risks, opportunities and dependencies across government\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003esignificant programmes\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ehow organisational and government digital and data outcomes and targets will be achieved\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ecapability and capacity requirements\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ehow the strategy is to be implemented\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ehow AI and automation will be adopted responsibly to improve public services, productivity and decision support while maintaining public trust\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe cross-government digital and data strategy shall be developed in collaboration with senior business leaders and government digital and data specialists across government. It shall be communicated to organisations and used to support decision making (see 4.4).\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eNote: For current cross-government digital, data and AI expectations, see relevant government digital and data strategy, policy and guidance. \u003csup id=\"fnref:4\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"#fn:4\" class=\"footnote\" rel=\"footnote\" role=\"doc-noteref\"\u003e[footnote 4]\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/sup\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eNote: For data and information, see the National Data Library. \u003csup id=\"fnref:5\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"#fn:5\" class=\"footnote\" rel=\"footnote\" role=\"doc-noteref\"\u003e[footnote 5]\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/sup\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch4 id=\"digital-strategy-and-planning-in-an-organisation\"\u003e4.2.2 Digital strategy and planning in an organisation\u003c/h4\u003e\u003cp\u003eEach organisation should define and implement a government digital and data strategy, which shall:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ealign to the cross-government digital and data strategy (see 4.2.1)\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ealign to the organisation’s policy and strategy\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ebe subject to approval by the accounting officer (see 4.6.3)\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eset out how AI will be used safely, lawfully, ethically and effectively, where relevant to organisational objectives\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe government digital and data strategy should be developed collaboratively by the organisation’s senior leaders and led by the senior officer accountable for the organisation’s government digital and data portfolio (see 4.6.4). It should reach at least three to five years into the future, and should:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eoutline the organisation’s ambition for how government digital and data capabilities will be used to achieve the organisation’s objectives\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003einclude benchmarks which enable assessment of the organisation’s current performance and effectiveness\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eoutline plans for how the organisation will achieve its objectives for digital services, data, technology and capability\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003edescribe the data, skills, governance and assurance needed to support responsible AI adoption\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe government digital and data strategy should be endorsed and actively supported by the accounting officer (see 4.6.3) and senior leadership, as this is critical to achieving effective digital transformation and better outcomes.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eA detailed plan for government digital and data activity should set out owners, milestones, dependencies, risks and key performance indicators. Where AI is used, the plan should also define the intended benefits, data requirements, human oversight, assurance approach, model or tool ownership, monitoring arrangements and route for escalating risks. Plans should be agreed with relevant senior leaders and reviewed through governance and performance reporting.\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"assurance\"\u003e4.3  Assurance\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp\u003eAssurance provides confidence to senior leaders and stakeholders that work is controlled, proportionate and supports successful delivery of policy, strategy and objectives.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eOrganisations should have a defined approach to assurance of government digital and data spend and activity. Assurance should be proportionate to risk, value and impact, integrated with the organisation’s overall assurance framework, and aligned to cross-government strategy, standards and expenditure controls.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eAI-enabled activity should be assured across its lifecycle, including use case selection, data quality, privacy, security, ethical risk, bias, transparency, human oversight, procurement, operational monitoring and retirement. Assurance should confirm that AI is used only where it is appropriate, lawful, secure and supported by the right skills and controls.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eTypically, assurance should be on at least three separate and defined levels, including:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eby, or on behalf of, the operational management team that owns and manages risk\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eby, or on behalf of, senior management, independent of operational management, using specialist expertise to oversee management of the risk, and to ensure the first line of defence is properly designed and operating as intended\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eby independent bodies to provide senior management with an objective opinion on the effectiveness of governance, risk management and internal controls, including the effectiveness of the previous lines of defence\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003eRecommendations provided through assurance processes should be incorporated into delivery planning at the earliest opportunity.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eNote: Organisations should consider relevant cross-government assurance regimes, including GovAssure and related assurance requirements. \u003csup id=\"fnref:6\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"#fn:6\" class=\"footnote\" rel=\"footnote\" role=\"doc-noteref\"\u003e[footnote 6]\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/sup\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eGovernment Functional Standard GovS 009: Internal Audit shall be complied with. \u003csup id=\"fnref:7\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"#fn:7\" class=\"footnote\" rel=\"footnote\" role=\"doc-noteref\"\u003e[footnote 7]\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/sup\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe requirements of the Orange Book: Management of Risk, Principles and Concepts, including Part II, the Risk Control Framework and its assurance expectations, shall be met. \u003csup id=\"fnref:8\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"#fn:8\" class=\"footnote\" rel=\"footnote\" role=\"doc-noteref\"\u003e[footnote 8]\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/sup\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"decision-making\"\u003e4.4  Decision making\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp\u003eDecisions relating to government digital and data activity should be made, approved and authorised in a timely way in accordance with the organisation’s governance and management framework. Where specified, minimum expectations shall be met (see 4.2.1).\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eOptions and decisions should be based on clear criteria, evidence and user needs, and informed by a proportionate analysis of benefits and uncertainty, including risks, opportunities, assumptions and dependencies, taking into account the chances of different degrees of success or failure.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eKey decisions relating to government digital and data activity should include:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ealignment to cross-government and organisational strategy and plans\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eauthorising programmes and projects (see Government Functional Standard GovS 002: Project Delivery)\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eefficiency and value\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003esustainability of options, including the purchase of products and services (see Government Functional Standard GovS 008: Commercial)\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003evalue for money, in alignment with Managing Public Money\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eresponsible use of AI, including lawfulness, ethics, data protection, transparency, explainability, human oversight, security, model performance and ongoing monitoring\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003eNo organisation should make decisions which impact other organisations without having consulted them.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eGovernment Functional Standard GovS 002: Project Delivery shall be complied with, with respect to portfolio, programme or project related decisions (such as initiating a project, authorising a new project phase, or responding to issues and risks).\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eGovernment Functional Standard GovS 008: Commercial shall be complied with, with respect to commercial decisions (such as deciding on a third-party supplier).\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eGovernment Functional Standard GovS 010: Analysis shall be complied with, with respect to the assessment of options.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eOrganisations shall comply with expenditure controls guidance. \u003csup id=\"fnref:9\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"#fn:9\" class=\"footnote\" rel=\"footnote\" role=\"doc-noteref\"\u003e[footnote 9]\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/sup\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eOrganisations shall comply with guidance on how to handle public funds. \u003csup id=\"fnref:10\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"#fn:10\" class=\"footnote\" rel=\"footnote\" role=\"doc-noteref\"\u003e[footnote 10]\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/sup\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"risk-management\"\u003e4.5 Risk management\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp\u003eRisk management supports informed decision making and helps digital products, services, data and technology operate successfully in support of objectives. It should address uncertainty, threats and opportunities, taking into account the chances of different degrees of success or failure. This includes risks arising from data, cyber security, legacy technology, third parties and AI.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe senior officer accountable for the organisation’s digital portfolio (see 4.6.4) should ensure that management of risk is:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eintegrated with the organisation’s overall risk management strategy\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003ewithin the organisation’s risk appetite and tolerance\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eproportionate to the scale and complexity of the work\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003eRisks associated with government digital and data activity should be represented at board level and reviewed regularly, including risks relating to sustainability of investment, continual improvement, capability, security, legacy technology, technical debt, data quality and AI use.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eDigital resilience risks shall be owned, monitored and reported through organisational governance arrangements.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eOrganisational contingency and business continuity planning should be defined for services where failure presents a clear risk to organisational objectives. Accountability for enacting disaster recovery plans should be defined.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe requirements of the Orange Book: management of risk - principles and concepts, shall be met. \u003csup id=\"fnref:3:1\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"#fn:3\" class=\"footnote\" rel=\"footnote\" role=\"doc-noteref\"\u003e[footnote 3]\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/sup\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"roles-and-accountabilities\"\u003e4.6  Roles and accountabilities\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ch4 id=\"overview-1\"\u003e4.6.1  Overview\u003c/h4\u003e\u003cp\u003eRoles and accountabilities shall be defined in governance and management frameworks and assigned to people with appropriate seniority, skills and experience.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eThis should include the activities, outputs or outcomes each role is responsible for, who they are accountable to, and how responsibilities are discharged for AI-enabled systems where relevant.\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch4 id=\"senior-officer-accountable-for-digital-strategy-and-planning-across-government\"\u003e4.6.2  Senior officer accountable for digital strategy and planning across government\u003c/h4\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe senior officer accountable for government digital and data strategy and planning across government is accountable for:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eproviding leadership and direction for government digital and data transformation and policy across government (see 3.2)\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003ecollaborating within the organisation to identify, assess and manage systemic digital, data and technology risks, and supporting collective action to address common vulnerabilities, dependencies and capability gaps\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003esetting and maintaining the cross-government governance and management framework (see 4.1)\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003edefining, communicating and implementing the cross-government digital and data strategy, policy and plans (see 4.2.1)\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003econtinuous improvement in the government’s use of digital services, technology and data to support improved outcomes (see sections 5, 6, 7 and digital practices in section 8)\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003esetting expectations for responsible AI adoption across government, including governance, assurance, transparency, capability and risk management\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003eNote: The Government Digital Service, part of the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport, leads the Government Digital and Data function for government.\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch4 id=\"accounting-officer\"\u003e4.6.3  Accounting officer\u003c/h4\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe permanent head of a government department is usually its principal accounting officer.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eAn organisation’s accounting officer is accountable (via a principal accounting officer where appropriate) to Parliament and the public for the stewardship of public resources, ensuring they are used effectively and to high standards of probity. The principal accounting officer generally appoints the most senior executive in the arm’s length bodies within the department’s ambit as an accounting officer.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe accounting officer is accountable for ensuring the organisation’s government digital and data strategy is appropriate (see 4.2.2), and should create an environment in which their organisation:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eendorses and actively supports government digital and data transformation\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eplans and manages government digital and data activity in accordance with this standard\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003euses AI responsibly and proportionately, with appropriate governance, assurance, transparency and human oversight\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003ch4 id=\"senior-officer-accountable-for-an-organisations-digital-portfolio\"\u003e4.6.4  Senior officer accountable for an organisation’s digital portfolio\u003c/h4\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe senior officer accountable for an organisation’s government digital and data portfolio is accountable to the accounting officer for:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eproviding leadership and direction for government digital and data transformation within the organisation\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eensuring government and organisational policies are complied with\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003esetting and maintaining the organisation’s governance and management framework (see 4.1)\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003esetting, communicating and implementing the organisation’s government digital and data strategy and plans (see 4.2)\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eensuring continuous improvement of government digital and data activity is a priority within the organisation\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003esupporting integrated management of digital and non-digital aspects of services, working with the senior officer accountable for service delivery (see 4.6.7)\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003emanaging government digital and data risk within the organisation’s risk appetite and tolerance (see 4.5)\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eensuring AI-related risks are identified, owned, assured and managed within the organisation’s risk appetite and legal obligations\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003ecollaborating within the organisation to identify, assess and manage systemic digital, data and technology risks, and supporting collective action to address common vulnerabilities, dependencies and capability gaps\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe senior officer accountable for an organisation’s government digital and data portfolio should be a member of the organisation’s senior decision-making forums to ensure that government digital and data priorities, risks and dependencies are represented.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eNote: In the majority of organisations this role is, but not limited to, a Director or Director General.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eNote: This role is often known as Chief Digital Officer or Chief Digital and Information Officer and would usually lead the organisation’s Government Digital and Data function.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eNote: See Government Functional Standard GovS 002: Project Delivery for more on portfolio, programme or project management.\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch4 id=\"senior-officer-accountable-for-data-in-an-organisation\"\u003e4.6.5  Senior officer accountable for data in an organisation\u003c/h4\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe senior officer accountable for data in an organisation is accountable to the senior officer accountable for the organisation’s government digital and data portfolio (see 4.6.4), for managing the organisation’s data and information assets, including data and information used to support AI-enabled systems, in relation to government digital and data activity.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe senior officer accountable for data is responsible for ensuring that the organisation:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eadopts and complies with relevant data, information governance and security requirements (see 4.1)\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003edevelops, maintains and implements a data and information strategy and plan (see 4.2)\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eassigns roles and responsibilities for the ownership, stewardship and management of data and information assets, including accountability for quality, access, retention, protection, reuse and remediation of issues\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eis enabled to use data and information to drive improvement in its productivity and services\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eensures data and information used for AI-enabled systems is suitable, lawful, secure, well-governed, appropriately documented and monitored for quality, provenance, bias, performance impact and drift\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003eIn large, complex organisations, where use of data relates to discrete business areas with different legal or security requirements, accountability for managing a subset of the organisation’s data may be separately delegated. In these cases, the data and information strategy and plan should explain how relevant interfaces are defined and managed.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eSee section 7, Data management.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eGovernment Functional Standard GovS 007: Security shall be complied with, with respect to data and information security. In line with this, organisations should consider appointing a data protection specialist role.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eNote: This role is often known as the Chief Data Officer.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eNote: This role might also be accountable to the senior officer accountable for analysis in an organisation for analysis related activity. See Government Functional Standard GovS 010: Analysis.\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch4 id=\"senior-officer-accountable-for-technology-in-an-organisation\"\u003e4.6.6  Senior officer accountable for technology in an organisation\u003c/h4\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe senior officer accountable for government digital and data in an organisation is accountable to the senior officer accountable for the organisation’s government digital and data portfolio (see 4.6.4), for managing the organisation’s government digital and data solutions (see section 6), and for ensuring that the organisation:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eadopts and complies with relevant government digital and data requirements and guidance (see 4.1)\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003edevelops, maintains and implements a government digital and data strategy and plan (see 4.2)\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eassigns appropriate roles and responsibilities for the ownership and management of government digital and data solutions\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003ehas an appropriate approach to technical security and resilience\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eensures AI-enabled solutions are designed, procured, implemented and monitored in line with security, resilience, ethics, assurance and data protection requirements\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003eThis role should provide technical direction for the design and delivery of services (see section 5), ensuring that government digital and data solutions, including AI-enabled solutions, are appropriate, cost-effective, scalable, secure, resilient and operationally sustainable.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eSee section 6, Government digital and data management.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eNote: This role is often known as the Chief Technology Officer. In large or complex organisations, it is often supported by a Chief Architect.\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch4 id=\"senior-officer-accountable-for-service-delivery\"\u003e4.6.7  Senior officer accountable for service delivery\u003c/h4\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe senior officer accountable for service delivery is accountable to the accounting officer for directing the integrated management of the organisation’s service delivery operations, ensuring that:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003ethe portfolio of services, including digital and non-digital elements, meets policy and organisational objectives\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003ethe organisation uses performance data and user feedback to understand how well services are performing in terms of usability and efficiency\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eAI or automation used in service delivery is transparent, monitored, explainable where appropriate, and subject to meaningful human oversight for significant decisions\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eaccountabilities and responsibilities for each service are assigned, with service owners taking end-to-end responsibility (see 4.6.8)\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eappropriate provision is made for users who are not using digital channels\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003eWhere an organisation’s portfolio of services is complex or very large, accountability for a sub-portfolio of services may be delegated (directly by the accounting officer, or from this role), provided the resulting user and product interfaces are defined and managed.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eNote: In a government department or large arm’s length body, with services comprising a mix of digital and non-digital components, it is likely that a Director General or Chief Operating Officer would be the appropriate person to undertake this role.\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch4 id=\"service-owner\"\u003e4.6.8  Service owner\u003c/h4\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe service owner is accountable to the senior officer accountable for service delivery (4.6.7) for the oversight and promotion of their assigned end-to-end service (see section 5), including:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003edeveloping and operating the service holistically (covering digital and any non-digital elements) to meet user needs, operate efficiently, and maintain required levels of performance (see 8.9)\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003emaintaining a service backlog to support the setting of priorities for continuous improvements, enhancements and updates\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eensuring necessary approval processes are followed, and risks and issues are mitigated (see 4.5)\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eensuring AI-enabled service changes are tested, monitored and assured before and after deployment\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003esecuring and managing costs and pricing, where appropriate\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003emanaging customer relations and responding to user feedback (see 8.6)\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eservice transition and retirement, where necessary\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe service owner is accountable for ensuring that relevant roles and responsibilities for delivery of the service are assigned and documented, and for the integrated management of the service across the multi-disciplinary delivery team.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe service owner should be supported by a digital service manager (see 4.6.9) to manage the specific digital aspects of the service. Where appropriate and justified, this role may be combined with the role of digital service manager to streamline operations, for example where a service is delivered only through digital channels.\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch4 id=\"digital-service-manager\"\u003e4.6.9  Digital service manager\u003c/h4\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe digital service manager is responsible for the development and day-to-day operation of the digital aspects of their assigned service (see section 5), and is accountable to the service owner for:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eensuring the digital service meets user needs (see 8.3)\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003emanaging digital content and design\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eplanning, tracking, reviewing and reporting on the operation of the digital service (see 5.4)\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eensuring there is useful and timely performance and management information data (see 5.6) on the services, and that this is consistent with cross-government standards\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eprioritising and managing workflow\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eresponding to and resolving problems, incidents and issues\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eescalating risks and issues as needed (see 4.5)\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003edelivering continuous improvements, enhancements and updates\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003e\n    \u003cp\u003eensuring any AI-assisted operational activity is appropriately monitored, reviewed and escalated where risks, inaccuracies or service impacts arise\u003c/p\u003e\n  \u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e"

      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "5. Service management",
      "url": "https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/government-functional-standard-govs-005-digital/government-functional-standard-govs-005-digital-html#service-management",

        "url": "https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/government-functional-standard-govs-005-digital/government-functional-standard-govs-005-digital-html#service-management",
        "text": "\u003ch3 id=\"overview-2\"\u003e5.1  Overview\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp\u003eThis section provides a framework for developing, managing, improving and, where needed, retiring services.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eServices should be digital where this best meets user needs, and should be developed and delivered by multi-disciplinary teams using agile methods.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eAccountability for the ownership and management of service delivery and each service shall be assigned (see 4.6.7 and 4.6.8).\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"policy-intent\"\u003e5.2  Policy intent\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp\u003ePolicy intent should be reflected in the organisation’s business strategy, business plan and service portfolio (see 5.5).\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eService outcomes, efficiencies and benefits should be defined and traceable to the achievement of, or support for, policy intent.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003ePolicy owners and those accountable for service delivery should work in cross-functional teams under a single service owner, so policy intent is reflected continuously.\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"service-design-and-development\"\u003e5.3  Service design and development\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp\u003eNew, changed or transformed services should provide value to government and users, and be usable and efficient. See GovS 002, Project delivery.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eServices shall be delivered in accordance with the Service Standard. \u003csup id=\"fnref:2:1\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"#fn:2\" class=\"footnote\" rel=\"footnote\" role=\"doc-noteref\"\u003e[footnote 2]\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/sup\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eUser research (see 8.3), iterative development and, where appropriate, testing of AI-enabled components should continue throughout the service life cycle.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eServices shall be monitored using consistent service performance measures (see 5.6), reviewed quarterly.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eWhere services are not digital, or perform poorly against usability and efficiency measures, the service owner should consider redesigning the service end-to-end.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eOrganisations buying off-the-shelf products, services or AI-enabled tools should ensure suppliers can meet user needs and relevant standards. See 6.3 and GovS 008, Commercial.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eGovernment Functional Standard GovS 007: Security shall be complied with by embedding cyber security into digital services, including any AI-enabled components, throughout the life cycle.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eNote: Advice and guidance about technology choices can be found in the Technology Code of Practice. \u003csup id=\"fnref:3:2\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"#fn:3\" class=\"footnote\" rel=\"footnote\" role=\"doc-noteref\"\u003e[footnote 3]\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/sup\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eNote: Where AI is used in a service, it should be used only where there is clear evidence of user need, with appropriate human oversight, assurance, transparency, security and monitoring.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eNote: The Service Manual includes advice on creating and running public services that meet the Service Standard. \u003csup id=\"fnref:11\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"#fn:11\" class=\"footnote\" rel=\"footnote\" role=\"doc-noteref\"\u003e[footnote 11]\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/sup\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"service-management-1\"\u003e5.4  Service management\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp\u003eServices should be documented so their architecture, components and connections are defined and understood. This should include:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003euser-facing and internal systems\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ethe people and the tasks they carry out to run the service\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eprocesses\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003edata flows, decision points and any AI-enabled components\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003eA target operating model should be developed and maintained for each service. It should set out the delivery approach (see 8.2), working practices and processes, people and skills, and the data, technology and AI capabilities needed to provide the service in line with government digital and data ways of working.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eIntegrated management should cover:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003edigital and non-digital components of a service\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ethe service and the wider system of systems of which it is part, including dependencies on other organisations that provide parts of the same user journey\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003eServices should be delivered and improved iteratively to meet changing user needs, developments in technology, including AI where appropriate, and changes in government policy, releasing value through frequent deployment cycles.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eService owners and teams should use qualitative and quantitative evidence, including performance analytics (see 5.6), user feedback, user research (see 8.3) and evidence from AI monitoring where relevant, to prioritise iterative delivery and improvement. Improvements should be managed through a single service backlog.\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"management-of-the-organisations-portfolio-of-services\"\u003e5.5  Management of the organisation’s portfolio of services\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp\u003eOrganisations should maintain a service catalogue so public-facing and internal services, technologies and AI-enabled capabilities are discoverable for use and possible reuse across the organisation and by other organisations.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe portfolio of services should be maintained to ensure:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003etechnology, data, AI-enabled and non-digital components are planned and managed as a unified and consistent system\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ethere is a consistent portfolio-wide view of material risks, opportunities, concentrations of risk, inter-service dependencies and systemic vulnerabilities, with clear ownership and escalation arrangements\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003euser journeys across multiple services are streamlined and deliver a consistent user experience\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ethere is a consistent view of performance and prioritisation, as well as dependencies between services\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003efeedback informs future design and delivery across the organisation’s services\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"performance-metrics-and-feedback\"\u003e5.6  Performance metrics and feedback\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe service owner should define and collect performance metrics, taking account of the cross-government performance framework and any additional assurance needed for AI-enabled components.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eService performance targets should be established, managed and aligned with cross-government performance metrics. They should include:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003edata on usability and efficiency of the service\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003emeeting defined service levels\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eaccuracy, reliability, bias, transparency and human oversight measures where AI is used\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003ePerformance against targets should be reported to senior leaders and stakeholders, and should meet requirements in the cross-government governance and management framework (see 4.1).\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"accessible-and-inclusive-services\"\u003e5.7  Accessible and inclusive services\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp\u003eAccessible and inclusive services ensure any potential user can use the service regardless of their personal characteristics, situation, capabilities or access needs, and has equal access and opportunity.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eDigital services shall be designed and managed to meet defined user abilities and accessibility requirements. Relevant legislation shall be identified and must be complied with, including where AI affects access, decisions, content or user support.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eThose accountable for service development and delivery should:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ebuild services that are intuitive to use, and present complicated information as simply as possible\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003econsider and address the barriers different groups of users might face when trying to use the service\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eencourage users to use digital services, while providing help, human support and non-digital alternatives for those without the skills or access to use the digital option\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003emake sure users know which channels are available to them\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003eNote: Guidance on making services inclusive can be found in the Service Manual. \u003csup id=\"fnref:11:1\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"#fn:11\" class=\"footnote\" rel=\"footnote\" role=\"doc-noteref\"\u003e[footnote 11]\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/sup\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eNote: The Service Standard sets requirements for accessibility, usability, consistency and efficiency. \u003csup id=\"fnref:2:2\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"#fn:2\" class=\"footnote\" rel=\"footnote\" role=\"doc-noteref\"\u003e[footnote 2]\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/sup\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eNote: Attention is drawn to the public sector accessibility regulations. \u003csup id=\"fnref:12\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"#fn:12\" class=\"footnote\" rel=\"footnote\" role=\"doc-noteref\"\u003e[footnote 12]\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/sup\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"service-retirement\"\u003e5.8  Service retirement\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe senior officer accountable for the organisation’s service delivery (see 4.6.7) may decide to retire a service, taking advice from the service owner. This might reflect changes in policy or user need, consolidation with another service, or replacement of legacy technology, including AI-enabled components where relevant.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eOnce the decision to retire a service has been taken, the service owner should:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003earchive or move relevant assets\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003einform and support the public or business users to migrate to any new service\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003econsider dependencies across and beyond the organisation’s service portfolio, including data, technology and AI dependencies\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eensure impacted stakeholders are engaged\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ereview and, where needed, decommission AI models, prompts, data pipelines and monitoring arrangements safely\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e"
      }

        "text": "\u003ch3 id=\"overview-3\"\u003e6.1  Overview\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp\u003eA senior officer accountable for government digital and data shall be assigned in each organisation (see 4.6.6).\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe senior officer should ensure insights, research, data, technology and emerging capabilities, including artificial intelligence (AI), inform the organisation’s strategy, architecture and asset management approach (see 8.8).\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eGovernment Functional Standard GovS 002: Project Delivery shall be complied with, with respect to work that is part of a portfolio, programme or project.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eAI should be considered as part of the wider government digital and data landscape where it supports user needs, public value, operational effectiveness or better decision-making. Any use of AI should be lawful, ethical, secure, transparent and subject to appropriate human oversight, assurance and risk management.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eRelevant strategy, policy and subject specific standards should be followed, including:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eThe Technology Code of Practice \u003csup id=\"fnref:3:3\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"#fn:3\" class=\"footnote\" rel=\"footnote\" role=\"doc-noteref\"\u003e[footnote 3]\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/sup\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eCloud First Strategy \u003csup id=\"fnref:13\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"#fn:13\" class=\"footnote\" rel=\"footnote\" role=\"doc-noteref\"\u003e[footnote 13]\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/sup\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eManaging Vendor Lock-in \u003csup id=\"fnref:14\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"#fn:14\" class=\"footnote\" rel=\"footnote\" role=\"doc-noteref\"\u003e[footnote 14]\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/sup\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eNational Institute of Standards and Technology \u003csup id=\"fnref:15\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"#fn:15\" class=\"footnote\" rel=\"footnote\" role=\"doc-noteref\"\u003e[footnote 15]\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/sup\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eCyber Essentials \u003csup id=\"fnref:16\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"#fn:16\" class=\"footnote\" rel=\"footnote\" role=\"doc-noteref\"\u003e[footnote 16]\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/sup\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"technology-development-and-maintenance\"\u003e6.2  Technology development and maintenance\u003c/h3\u003e\u003cp\u003eDigital and data architecture sets the parameters for the configuration, interaction and interdependence of the components, services, data assets and systems that enable government digital and data solutions.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eArchitecture should align with the relevant target operating model, service needs and data requirements (see 5.4 and 8.4).\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eDigital and data architecture should reflect the organisation’s government digital and data strategy, support current and future service delivery, and remain deliverable within the organisation’s risk appetite (see 4.5).\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eIn keeping with the published standards (see 6.1), government digital and data solutions should:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ebe secure by design\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003euse open standards and open code\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eadhere to relevant classification standards\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eprotect data at rest and in transit\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003einclude appropriate governance, assurance and lifecycle controls where AI capabilities are used\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003eGovernment digital and data products, services and systems should be understood and actively managed. Governance controls should reduce legacy technology, manage technical debt, track cross-government alignment, understand supplier and supply-chain dependencies, and avoid unnecessary duplication. Controls should also cover business continuity, resilience and, where AI is used, model performance, data quality, bias, security, transparency, accountability and ongoing assurance.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eOrganisations should identify, document and manage risks and dependencies, including external dependencies and supply chains, especially where shared services, shared data arrangements or AI-enabled capabilities are in place (see 4.5).\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eGovernment digital and data solutions may be developed and managed in-house, by third-party suppliers, or through a combination of both. Where AI components are procured, built or integrated, roles, responsibilities, assurance requirements and supplier obligations should be defined from the outset (see 4.5).\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"deployment-and-operation-of-technology\"\u003e6.3  Deployment and operation of technology\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ch4 id=\"overview-4\"\u003e6.3.1  Overview\u003c/h4\u003e\u003cp\u003eEach organisation should have mechanisms for managing and continually improving its government digital and data solutions, so that changing business, policy, operational and user needs continue to be met.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eRelevant roles and responsibilities should be defined and assigned to reflect the organisation’s build or buy choices, including responsibility for AI-enabled components where applicable (see 4.5).\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eGovernment Functional Standard GovS 007: Security shall be complied with, with respect to a mechanism being in place for identifying and resolving security vulnerabilities.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eNote: For buy (third-party delivery), responsibilities are defined in the contract; for build (in-house delivery) see Technology Code of Practice guidance. \u003csup id=\"fnref:3:4\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"#fn:3\" class=\"footnote\" rel=\"footnote\" role=\"doc-noteref\"\u003e[footnote 3]\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/sup\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch4 id=\"operations-management\"\u003e6.3.2  Operations management\u003c/h4\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe senior officer accountable for government digital and data (see 4.6.6) should ensure those managing digital and data solutions have the capability, capacity and defined processes to run, operate and continuously improve them.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eProcesses should be defined and managed, and responsibility assigned for:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eensuring clean, secure and maintainable code for the organisation\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003emaintaining, iterating, and patching solutions against known vulnerabilities\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eunderstanding, identifying and remediating potential risks, with effective operational monitoring, including relevant service management processes such as incident management, problem management and disaster recovery\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eensuring consistent and tested business continuity arrangements are in place and understood by all stakeholders\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003emonitoring AI-enabled components where used, including performance, drift, data quality, security risks, explainability, human oversight and escalation routes\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003ch4 id=\"triggers-for-change\"\u003e6.3.3  Triggers for change\u003c/h4\u003e\u003cp\u003eTriggers for change should be understood and managed. They are likely to relate to:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003einternally generated change derived from operating digital and data solutions, including user feedback, data insights and performance metrics\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eexternally generated change derived from a new or updated policy, a public announcement, supplier expiry or another external reason\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003echange generated from decisions taken about the organisation’s digital and data architecture (see 6.2)\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003echanges in AI capability, regulation, risk profile, model performance, data quality or assurance requirements\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003eAddressing triggers for change might result in incremental change, service improvement, technical remediation, or upgrades managed through a project or programme.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe organisation’s legacy technology, data stores, digital services and AI-enabled components should be defined and monitored. An up-to-date plan should be maintained to remediate, replace or retire them.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eTechnology, data stores, digital services or AI-enabled components become legacy when they meet any of the following conditions:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003econsidered an end-of-life product\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eout of support or on extended support from the supplier\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eimpossible to update\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eno longer cost-effective\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003econsidered to be above the acceptable risk threshold\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eno longer meet required levels of assurance, explainability, data quality, security or human oversight\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003ch3 id=\"retirement-of-government-digital-and-data-solutions\"\u003e6.4  Retirement of government digital and data solutions\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ch4 id=\"overview-5\"\u003e6.4.1  Overview\u003c/h4\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe purpose of retirement is to ensure government digital and data solutions remain fit for purpose. A solution should be considered for retirement if:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eit is not possible to update or improve the existing solution to meet future business, policy, operational or user needs\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ethere are resource constraints\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ethe solution represents poor value for money\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ethere is a reduction or ending of future supplier support\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eidentified risks are unacceptably high\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eit is incompatible with the ambition set by the organisation’s government digital and data strategy\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eAI-enabled components can no longer be assured, monitored, explained, secured or controlled to an acceptable standard\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe senior officer accountable for government digital and data in an organisation (see 4.6.6) should:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eidentify components, systems, data stores or services that are no longer capable of meeting the organisation’s needs\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eidentify the services or business operations that rely on the solution intended for retirement\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003econsult service owners, data owners and other stakeholders that rely on the existing solution, to understand their priorities for future operation\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eassess whether any AI-enabled components, models, training data, prompts, outputs, logs or derived data need to be retained, migrated, archived or deleted\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eoversee service delivery teams to ensure the management and retirement of the solution and, where necessary, its replacement, meets the organisation’s needs\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ework with service owners and stakeholders to ensure all data is migrated, archived or removed in line with data protection, classification and information assurance requirements\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003elead the removal and appropriate disposal of retired technology, systems and data assets\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003eNecessary replacement arrangements should be in place before retirement takes place.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eNote: Retire includes withdrawal from existing services or operations, and disposal of associated technology, systems, data assets and AI-enabled components.\u003c/p\u003e\u003ch4 id=\"withdraw-technology\"\u003e6.4.2  Withdraw technology\u003c/h4\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe process and complexity of moving away from legacy systems, data stores, technologies and AI-enabled components varies depending on the solution involved.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eNote: For example, decommissioning physical hardware such as laptops is more straightforward than decommissioning a mainframe and building a replacement system in the cloud.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eBefore a solution is withdrawn, the following actions should be taken:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003ereview existing contractual arrangements and take any necessary action to end the contract, if appropriate\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eprepare data that is to be migrated\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eplan transition of services to alternative solutions, if required\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003edefine and implement a secure process for migrating data between systems, or data removal and destruction based on the information assurance needs and any GDPR data associated with the system\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003econfirm whether any AI models, configuration, prompts, outputs, logs, training data or evaluation records need to be retained, transferred, archived or securely destroyed\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eengage with staff and other users affected by the change, and provide necessary training or guidance\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003ch4 id=\"dispose-of-technology-systems-and-data-assets\"\u003e6.4.3  Dispose of technology, systems and data assets\u003c/h4\u003e\u003cp\u003eThe service owner (see 4.6.8) and the senior officer accountable for government digital and data in an organisation (see 4.6.6) should ensure redundant equipment, systems, data assets and AI-enabled components are appropriately disposed of.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eDisposal shall meet security requirements, and any physical hardware disposal should, where possible, be recycled using recognised and sustainable approaches.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eWhen decommissioning cloud-based assets or AI-enabled services, processes should ensure residual data, models, logs, outputs and configuration are not accessible post-disposal. Relevant security guidance should always be considered when disposing of technology.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eRequirements for the handling of personal data being moved or removed must be followed in accordance with prevailing regulations and security advice, including where personal data has been used in AI-enabled systems.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eNote: Attention is drawn to the following requirements:\u003c/p\u003e\u003cul\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eUK General Data Protection Regulation (UK GDPR) \u003csup id=\"fnref:17\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"#fn:17\" class=\"footnote\" rel=\"footnote\" role=\"doc-noteref\"\u003e[footnote 17]\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/sup\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n  \u003cli\u003eThe Data Protection Act \u003csup id=\"fnref:18\"\u003e\u003ca href=\"#fn:18\" class=\"footnote\" rel=\"footnote\" role=\"doc-noteref\"\u003e[footnote 18]\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/sup\u003e\n\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\u003cp\u003eGovernment Functional Standard GovS 007: Security shall be complied with when disposing of technology, systems, data assets and AI-enabled components.\u003c/p\u003e\u003cp\u003eWhere AI-enabled components are retired or disposed of, organisations should ensure models, prompts, outputs, logs, training data, evaluation records and configuration are handled in line with data protection, security, information assurance and retention requirements.\u003c/p\u003e"
